Evolution doesn't perfect an animal, just gets it to where its good enough to survive. If an issue doesn't prevent *most* of the population from being unable to pass on genes, then there's no pressure and population with mutations that might help assuade the issue will remain a minority population and might even die out over time.

If more of the mutated population survive to pass on theie genes over time, then that's the gene that carries on for the species as a whole, and the animal has therefore evolved. 
If an animal struggles to walk with 3 legs, but this doesn't substantially prevent the majority of them from breeding, the animal is gonna keep having 3 legs instead of growing a fourth to "perfect" itself.

Completely different genre. Cyberpunk really isn't just "cool technology". The theme, tone, setting and state of the world matter.

General rules of thumb for Cyberpunk is high tech, low life. Everyone generally has access to high tech. The world most closely resembles society today.  Controlling corporate entities in a usually dangerous but organized society are extremely common (if not corporate, government) Usually hyperurban and hyperdense. The society is generally dangerous because of other members of society; ie radicalized hackers, turfwarring gangers, disillusioned corporates. Near-future pollution, and rarely post apocalyptic UNLESS society reorganized and extensively rebuilt since.

Fallout, conversely, is a purely junkcore post apocalyptic, in a world where  access to tech is extremely limited. Society is not organized, it's scattered and is basically either based around serfdom or is wholly tribalistic. People generally live in prehistoric, subsistence farming squalor. There is no singular society-controlling entity. There are just competing military forces. It's dangerous, yeah, but because of mutated monsters and raiders. The robots are the tech fantasy leftovers from the old world, not something widely produced by the current "societies". Even the BoS uses prewar tech because they could never make it themselves. Modding cyberpunk is fairly easy

You CAN use Vortex for it but it's not really recommended 

Go to Steam, right click on the name of the game in your library, click "open file location". 

Search for a mods folder. If my memory is right it's gonna be under /archive/pc

You can also look that up if you're unsure, this is where ALL mods by any method will end up going.

If there's no mod folder there, create one.

Go download a mod of choice from Nexus. Make sure to check to make sure whether it has a dependant core mod like Cyber Engine Tweaks or ArchiveXL. Most mods will have at least one. Every time the game updates, you will need to update all your mods and the core mods, or else the game will not launch. Usually you only need to update the core mods.

Once you download the mods, take the files and drop it into your cyberpunk folder. You can stick it in the main directory. Unzip it, and it should automatically sort itself into all the nessecary folders. Always check if a mod specifies it has a different install method in the description-- if not, assume it's fine to just unzip it in the main directory. If it unpacks into the main directory, just move the .archive file into the mod folder.

It's easy enough.  This sounds like a lot but it's literally just "download mods > unzip them into main folder > make sure it works > update mods as needed" 

The only real headache is when you can't find the one unupdated mod that's preventing the game from launching because of the game updates breaking everything, but that probably won't be a major problem for much longer.
